chunks: Stick to the earth, and be patient in trials,
and do not move your hands and swords according to the liking of your tongues,
and do not hasten in matters in which Allah has not hastened for you,

for whoever among you dies on his bed while he has knowledge of the right of his Lord, Exalted and Glorified, and the right of His Messenger and the members of His House, may the prayers of Allah be upon him and upon them, will die as a martyr,
and his reward is incumbent on Allah,
and he earns the reward of what he intended of his good deeds,
and his intention takes the place of drawing his sword,
for indeed, for every thing there is a time and a limit.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of intention and patience in achieving martyrdom according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In the context of the era of quietism following the Battle of Siffin, Imam Ali advises believers to preserve their faith through patience and intellectual conviction rather than engaging in premature political uprisings driven by rhetorical passion. This hadith establishes the theological principle that sincere intention (niyyah) and correct knowledge (ma'rifah) of the Ahl al-Bayt can suffice for martyrdom, elevating the status of the 'silent believer' to that of the warrior. It underscores the Shia concept of waiting for the divinely appointed time (ajal) for justice, prioritizing spiritual readiness over hasty physical action.
